title: 鸟鸣涧
author: 王维
intro: A night so still you can hear osmanthus petals fall, until the rising moon startles a bird into song. Wang Wei uses a few small sounds to make silence audible.
analysis: 这首诗写春天夜里山谷的寂静。第一句“人闲桂花落”：人心闲下来，才能注意到细小的桂花一朵朵落下。第二句“夜静春山空”，整座山好像空了。后两句很妙：月亮升起来，月光竟然惊醒了山里的鸟，它们不时在山涧里叫几声。鸟叫本来是声音，为什么反而让人觉得更静？因为只有在非常安静的环境里，月光这样轻的变化才会惊动鸟儿，几声鸟鸣也才听得这么清楚。这种手法叫“以动衬静”——用声音和动作来衬托安静。王维信佛，这首诗里的“闲”和“空”，也带着他内心的平和。
analysisEn: A spring night in a mountain ravine. The first line links person and scene: only when your mind is at rest (闲) can you notice osmanthus flowers — tiny ones — dropping one by one. The second line widens the view: the night is still, and the whole spring mountain feels empty. The last two lines are the surprise. The moon rises, and its light is enough to startle the sleeping birds, which call out now and then in the ravine. Why does birdsong make the night feel quieter, not noisier? Because only in deep silence could something as soft as moonlight wake a bird, and only in silence would a few calls carry so clearly. Chinese critics call this “using movement to set off stillness” (以动衬静): a small sound makes you notice the quiet around it, like one ripple on a still pond. Wang Wei was a devout Buddhist, and the words 闲 (at ease) and 空 (empty) also suggest the calm of his own mind.
background: Wang Wei (701–761), poet, painter and Buddhist. This is the first of five short poems he wrote on scenes at Yunxi (“Cloud Stream”), the country home of his friend Huangfu Yue.
pronunciation: 涧 jiàn（山间的小溪，不读 jiān）。
version: 采用通行的教材版本，原为《皇甫岳云溪杂题五首》的第一首。

lines.lit: People at leisure; osmanthus flowers fall;
lines.en: My mind at rest, I hear the osmanthus fall;

lines.lit: the night is still; the spring mountain is empty.
lines.en: the night is still, the spring hills empty.

lines.lit: The moon comes out and startles the mountain birds;
lines.en: The rising moon startles the mountain birds,

lines.lit: now and then they sing in the spring ravine.
lines.en: and now and then they call across the spring ravine.

words.note: 一种很香的小花，现代汉语也用，如“桂花糕”。
古义；现代汉语说“时时”“不时”。

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 桂花又小又轻，连它落下都能察觉，可见人心多闲、夜多静。
imagery.en: Osmanthus flowers are tiny; noticing them fall shows how calm the mind and how quiet the night.

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: “春山空”写出整座山的空寂，也是诗人内心的平静。
imagery.en: “The spring hills empty” is the mountain’s silence and the poet’s inner calm.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 月光轻轻升起，竟能惊动山鸟，反衬山中极静。
imagery.en: The moon rising is enough to startle the birds — proof of how silent the hills are.

imagery.name: 鸟
imagery.zh: 几声鸟鸣打破寂静，却让人更觉得安静（以动衬静）。
imagery.en: A few bird calls break the silence yet make it feel deeper — sound setting off stillness.
